notes: Deep-agent RUN LIMITS (llm_agents/deep_agents/limits.py::run_limits) — how many and how large the LLM requests of one run may be. max_conversation_steps: the per-conversation hop budget the bridge/server defaults to (one LLM turn may call tools; the budget bounds turns). min_conversation_steps / max_steps_cap: the execute-node clamp on whatever a run asked for (a delegated spawn gets +8 headroom under the same cap). recursion_limit: the LangGraph superstep bound for one graph invocation (plan + hops + replans + finalize + result). run_timeout_sec: the run's TOTAL wall-clock budget — the step lane checks it every hop and routes to finalize at the budget (the bridge's and the browser client's deadlines sit at the same value). llm_request_timeout_sec: the per-LLM-request wall-clock budget — the provider transport's retry ladder terminates at the budget (each attempt's read timeout shrinks to the remainder; the per-attempt read cap is the transport's 120s, so a larger budget buys MORE FRESH ATTEMPTS — the rescue for the provider's intermittent single-request hangs, 2026-11-03: two runs lost review-wave requests at 300s ≈ 2 attempts, raised to 600s ≈ 5); an overrun means the input is too heavy for one call and the caller refactors it into smaller tasks (the planner's slimmed init; the spawn pre-planner's small call), never a same-payload retry. The budget bounds ONE individual LLM request (one chat completion, retries included) — NOT a graph node: a node (one step conversation hop) makes many such requests across its tool turns and legitimately outlasts this budget many times over; nodes are bounded by max_conversation_steps and the run by run_timeout_sec instead. max_plan_nodes / max_delegated_steps: the planned plan's step count and how many of those may be delegated spawns. plan_repair_rounds: the planning session's propose-to-correct rounds per batch. plan_proposal_batches: the batched proposal protocol's round cap — the first call proposes the first few steps, every later round proposes the next batch over the nodes-so-far (each a small LLM call that persists immediately; the plan closes when the model replies more:false), so planning never hangs on one giant reply. max_total_plan_steps / max_spawn_children: the replan guards (update_plan total nodes, spawns per node). max_parallel_delegated_steps: the spawn-wave width per hop (the parallel wave is LangGraph's parallel-join semantics: consecutive delegated-or-parallel steps run concurrently and the NEXT merge node — the first unmarked inline step, normally the custom graph's synthesis step — starts only after EVERY member settles, failed members included). max_concurrent_subagents: the per-agent spawn semaphore. max_spawn_depth: spawn-chain depth (an agent at the depth carries no spawn tool). subagent_timeout_sec: wall clock per spawned child, null = unbounded. max_output_tokens: the per-LLM-request output ceiling (the runaway guard). max_output_repairs: output-validation repair rounds per conversation. finding_max_chars / findings_block_max_chars: the findings bridge's per-finding and whole-block caps (older findings age to title lines past the block cap). prompt_eager_rows / prompt_eager_chars: the eager skill-loading budget before the planner's verdict decides. prompt_hotpath_rows / hotpath_probe_chains: the KG-HOTPATH corroboration lane (planning/kg_prompts.py, 2026-11-07) — optional-labeled skills the PROMOTED llm.kg_hotpaths chains implicate (the run's question trigram-matches a promoted query; the chain's ns1 entities name the skill or its optional labels hit the chain's bilingual entity vocabulary) auto-load at plan time, at most prompt_hotpath_rows rows per run (0 disables the lane — bound-label rows always load regardless), probing at most hotpath_probe_chains top-hit_count chains. data_hints_rows: the MATERIALIZED-DATA hints (langgraph/runner/base.py, 2026-11-09) — each step hop's directive is KG-searched (read-only table_hits over the TTL-cached ns0 graph) and the surfaced analysis tables ride the step message as a load-before-compute block naming the tables, at most data_hints_rows of them (0 disables the lane). payload_guard_chars / payload_entry_max_chars / payload_preview_chars / payload_preview_items: the LARGE-PAYLOAD PRE-CHECK (llm_agents/deep_agents/payload_guard.py) at every message builder — a structured-context subtree whose serialized size passes payload_entry_max_chars ships as _guarded metadata + preview (payload_preview_chars per value, payload_preview_items per container) with a prompt block naming what was elided so the model re-fetches and checks the real data through its tools; payload_guard_chars is the whole-block gate that trims the largest remaining top-level entries down to it. tool_result_max_chars: the head+tail cap on ONE tool result's text before it enters the conversation transcript. Takes effect on the NEXT run — the daemon re-reads per run, no restart needed. supervisor_poll_interval_sec / supervisor_repair_grace_sec / supervisor_max_node_retries / supervisor_max_repairs_per_run: the SUPERVISOR REPAIR LANE (2026-11-06) — the per-run backend poller watches node states while the graph runs; on a root-path step failure the step lane opens a bounded pause window (the grace) for the supervisor agent's verdict, and a transient error (rate limit, timeout, upstream 5xx) within both retry budgets gets its failed row re-opened and the hop re-run. grace 0 disables repair (the lane never waits); healthy runs pay one cheap DB poll per interval and zero LLM. supervisor_retry_throttle_sec: the cooldown a rate-limit-class retry waits INSIDE the repair pause window before the hop re-runs (2026-11-06: immediate re-runs re-hit the account rate limit; grace 120 covers intervention + 45). supervisor_cap_retries_per_run / supervisor_cap_retry_step_bump: the CAP-CLASS RETRY LANE (2026-11-15, run d7b24a36) — a step-cap death whose error text's embedded usage counters show real work (>= 5 tool calls, repair.CAP_RETRY_MIN_TOOL_CALLS) is retried at most supervisor_cap_retries_per_run times per run, and the retried node's fresh conversation (and its delegated spawn children) runs under the hop's normal clamp + supervisor_cap_retry_step_bump steps (deliberately ABOVE max_steps_cap — that excess is the lane's point); 0 retries or a 0 bump disables the lane; a cap death with little recorded work stays no-action. sandbox_failure_nudge_threshold / sandbox_failure_max_nudges: the WRITE-RUN-FIX loop breaker (core/loop/breaker.py + core/loop/run.py, 2026-11-11) — after sandbox_failure_nudge_threshold consecutive failed sandbox-tool outcomes (a hard tool error, or a sandbox_run exiting non-zero) the conversation gets ONE user nudge teaching patch-the-broken-block (sandbox_edit_file) + fail-fast per-block try/except; at most sandbox_failure_max_nudges per conversation, 0 disables the breaker. sandbox_spawn_after_failures / sandbox_spawn_max: the breaker's FRESH-CONTEXT ESCALATION (2026-11-11) — after sandbox_spawn_after_failures consecutive TRACEBACK-class script failures (exit non-zero with a Traceback/SyntaxError in the output; timeouts never count) the loop spawns ONE repair subagent the parent AWAITS (foreground, through the same hooks a model-called spawn rides — the child state row registers in the plan tree), whose whole context is the compact handoff (run goal + script path + the failed runs' exception lines + method) instead of the parent's grown transcript; the child's answer rides back as an injection user message and both streaks reset; at most sandbox_spawn_max per conversation (0 disables the spawn lane). Both built for the run-e1c366bd failure mode: nine whole-script rewrites chasing eight SQL bugs until the user stopped the run. Python-only knobs (no Run-Limits-panel field — a panel save rewrites this file from the TS whitelist and would drop unlisted keys, the pre-existing prompt_hotpath_rows hazard). preview_batch_rows / preview_stats_sample_rows / preview_jev_classify: the PREVIEW ENVELOPE knobs (llm_agents/_core/preview.py via payload_guard.py, 2026-11-12 — replaced the _guarded stubs): the head/mid/tail ROW batches one data envelope carries, the row sample the per-column mean/std/min/max run over, and the loop seam's soft jev read (sentiment / domain / industries, langgraph decision content_* templates) riding large TEXT tool results — JEV_PREVIEW=0 is that read's env kill-switch, it needs an injected decision engine. PYTHON-ONLY KEYS (no Run-Limits-panel field — a panel save rewrites this file from the TS whitelist and would drop unlisted keys). jev_route / jev_route_max_spawns / jev_route_join / jev_route_probe_max: THE SYSTEM ONE ROUTER (core/loop/router.py, 2026-11-12) — after every LLM response the injected jev engine routes the NEXT work: inference (continue) / spawn (a fresh scripting sub node takes over proposed sandbox script work; never inside a scripting node) / join (a messy scripting node stops and hands back to the parent chain); jev_route_max_spawns bounds router spawns per conversation (0 disables the spawn lane), jev_route_join gates the join lane, jev_route_probe_max bounds the failure-probe investigator spawns (a failed scripting child joins back and the parent spawns an AUTHORIZED investigator — the failed node's state id / llm chain id / context refs handed to it — on every jev read except a confident no; JEV_ROUTE=0 is the env kill-switch). jev_route_fork / jev_route_max_forks: the router's FORK lane (core/loop/router.py, 2026-11-13) — when the spawn read says the proposed sandbox coding is a CONTINUATION of this conversation's own chain (not self-contained), a second noul read offers the fork: a sub node that INHERITS this conversation's full transcript continues the coding while the parent awaits (foreground); jev_route_max_forks bounds router forks per conversation (0 disables the fork lane). fork_inherit_max_messages: the fork child's inherited-transcript cap — beyond it the child keeps the first user message (the run goal) plus the most recent turns with an elision marker (0 disables the cap). PYTHON-ONLY KEYS.
